chapter: Cab Calloway, Harlem and New York musicians
title: The trombone players in the basement: Higginbotham, Herb Gregory, Wilson
summary: Danny names the trombonists present that morning and notes Herb Gregory's skill, Herb Flemming being in Europe, and Wilson's challenges.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Sure. Well, who all was on that? Who was in there that morning?

Higgenbotham. Herb Gregory. He was always starting something. Herb Gregory was a trombone player who could play. He was partly a boozer, but he was on time. But he had something about him. He drank so much that every time you spoke to him there was whiskey on his breath, see. So that annoyed some leaders, I guess. And he looked red-eyed. But the man could play a whole lot of trombone. That's somebody that they overlook.
And who else was in there...?
Old Herb Flemming didn't happen to be around there, did he?
No, Herb Flemming was in Europe. He hadn't come back. He came back later. This is around 1932. Sandy Williams.

There was about seven trombone players there. Wilson was in there. Wilson was the West Indian trombone player. He was always getting in it, and he'd want to start something. "I've got something new, something that nobody has ever heard before." And it would be "Margie" in another key. Well, that was the challenge like of New York. You
can go in there for hours about that, who was on first and who was on second...
